skill.name: checkpoint
skill.description: Mid-session save point: create a descriptive git commit and a brief handoff note, then keep working. Use before a risky change or refactor, when switching tasks, or to bank progress without ending the session. Triggers on: /checkpoint, "checkpoint", "save progress", "commit and handoff", "save state", "pause here", "before a risky change". For the full end-of-session ritual with learning extraction, use /wrap-up instead.
skill.summary: Save current progress with a local Git commit and an abbreviated handoff note, then continue working.
skill.author: codewithmukesh

content.user_title: Save Progress with Git Checkpoints and Handoff Notes
content.value_statement: Task switches and risky refactors can interrupt progress and leave important context behind. This skill guides a local Git checkpoint and brief handoff before work continues.
actual_capabilities: Inspect staged and unstaged changes with Git status and diff.
Stage specific relevant files while excluding secrets, generated files, and build artifacts.
Create a new descriptive commit using the repository commit style, without amending existing commits.
Overwrite .claude/handoff.md with completed work, pending steps, optional learnings, branch, and commit context.
Update only the handoff when there are no changes to commit.
Report the commit hash and handoff summary before continuing work.
limitations: Requires an assistant with local Git and file-writing permissions.
Does not push commits or modify remote branches.
Overwrites the existing handoff note rather than maintaining a note history.
Does not mandate running tests; a checkpoint alone does not prove correctness.

use_cases.title: Prepare for a Refactor
use_cases.description: Record current implementation progress and the next refactor step before making a risky change.

use_cases.title: Switch Maintenance Tasks
use_cases.description: Save focused changes and pending investigation details before moving to another issue.

use_cases.title: Resume Interrupted Work
use_cases.description: Leave branch, commit, completed work, and next steps for a later coding session.

prompt_templates.title: Save Current Progress
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checkpoint of my current work and summarize the handoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: save a completed unit of work.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for a Risky Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Checkpoint the current changes before refactoring [component]. Record [next step] as pending work and report the commit hash.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: establish a local commit before a refactor.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Task Switch
prompt_templates.prompt: Checkpoint relevant changes for [current task]. Leave [remaining steps] in the handoff before switching to [next task].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: preserve context across task changes.

prompt_templates.title: Checkpoint a Mixed Working Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Review staged and unstaged changes for [task]. Stage only [approved files], leave unrelated work untouched, and checkpoint with [next steps] in the handoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: constrain the checkpoint when multiple tasks share a working tree.

output_examples.input: Checkpoint the validation changes before the query refactor.
output: Checkpoint created with a new local commit for the validation changes.
Handoff updated with completed validation work and the pending query refactor.
Current branch and commit recorded. No remote changes made.

output_examples.input: Save progress when there are no changes to commit.
output: No changes to commit; no new commit created.
Handoff updated with pending work and current branch and commit context.

best_practices: Review the diff and staged files before committing; exclude secrets, generated files, and unrelated changes.
Use a focused commit message and record specific pending steps in the handoff.
Run relevant checks before treating a checkpoint as a known-good state.
anti_patterns: Staging the entire working tree without reviewing file scope.
Treating a local checkpoint as a remote backup or proof that tests pass.
Keeping unique historical context only in a handoff note that will be overwritten.

faq.question: What does a checkpoint save?
faq.answer: It creates a local Git commit for relevant changes and writes a brief handoff with progress and repository context.

faq.question: Does it push changes to a remote?
faq.answer: No. The instructions prohibit pushes, force-pushes, and changes to remote branches.

faq.question: What happens when there is nothing to commit?
faq.answer: It skips creating a commit and updates the handoff note only.

faq.question: Where is the handoff stored?
faq.answer: It is stored in .claude/handoff.md. Each checkpoint overwrites the previous note.

faq.question: Does checkpoint run the test suite?
faq.answer: The workflow does not require test execution. Run relevant checks before relying on the saved state.

faq.question: How does checkpoint differ from wrap-up?
faq.answer: Checkpoint saves progress and continues work. The referenced wrap-up workflow ends a session with a fuller handoff and learning extraction.
